title: Pitcher Reports
text: These internal pitcher reports are created and sent to our pitching coaches after every game. The script uses a TrackMan file to produce one PDF where each pitcher who appeared gets his own one-page report. They tell our coaches how hitters performed against our pitcher, how well he located his pitches, what his release on each pitch looked like, the shape of each pitch, and how his stuff compares to the average mid-major D1 arm. Generating reports for the full staff takes just a few minutes. The same script runs on a single game or on a combined file.

title: Pitcher Reports
text:
What’s on the page

Hitter Performance: BAA, exit velocity, ground-ball and fly-ball rates, and swing, whiff and chase rates, all by batter handedness.
Pitch Location vs RHH / LHH: every pitch plotted on the zone from the pitcher’s view, colored by pitch type.
Pitch Location Breakdown: strike rate for each pitch, plus how often it landed in the heart of the zone, the shadow of the zone, the chase area, or wasted.
Release Slot: the pitcher’s average release point drawn on a silhouette scaled to his height and arm slot, with each pitch type’s release point marked.
Pitch Movement: traditional pitch plot using IVB and HB with the mid-major D1 average for that pitch type and handedness included for comparison.
Pitch Characteristics: usage, velocity, spin rate and direction, induced vertical and horizontal break, release height and side, extension, and approach angle for each pitch.

title: Pitcher Reports
text:
How it works
The script reads a raw TrackMan CSV and keeps only our pitchers. Names are matched to the roster in a way that ignores stray spaces and capitalization to handle improper tagging. If a pitcher isn’t on the roster (say a potential recruit), the script asks for his arm slot and height to create his release slot diagram.
A few decisions that took some thought:

Mid-major averages. The mid-major averages are calculated using TrackMan data from teams in the Big West, Mountain West, and West Coast conferences.
Location bands. Each band is a fixed distance around a standard strike zone (17 inches wide, 1.5 to 3.5 feet high). Heart is the zone itself, Shadow extends 3 inches beyond each boundary, Chase extends 8 inches wide and 6 inches up and down, and anything beyond that is considered Waste. Pitches are classified based on where they crossed the front of the plate.
Keeping the location plots readable. In cumulative reports, pitchers can have hundreds of pitches tracked making the location plot unreadable. When there are more than 60, the script takes a sample and matches the each pitch types’ usage against each handedness. The full counts are still used in every table.
Accounting for ABs/PAs correctly. TrackMan records strikeouts, walks, and hit by pitches in the KorBB column while all balls in play are recorded under PlayResult. The script accounts for this and keeps just one result-bearing pitch per plate appearance to ensure rates are calculated correctly.

title: Pitcher Reports
text:
Impact
These reports are produced postgame and sent to our pitching coaches to look over. The next day one of our pitching coaches reviews the report with each pitcher and walks through the takeaways from the outing. Bullpen plans often get rearranged depending on the takeaways. If our pitching coach isn’t satisfied with the shape of a pitcher’s breaking ball, he might call for a pitch design pen on the TrackMan. If he isn’t happy with a pitcher’s fastball command, it might be an execution bullpen day. The reports are used to evaluate the performance and guide the development of our pitchers.

title: Pitcher Reports
text:
Code
One of the trickier pieces was the usage-weighted sampling for the location plots:


Show code

def sample_zone_pitches(sub, cap=MAX_ZONE_PITCHES, seed=ZONE_SAMPLE_SEED):
    """If there are more than `cap` located pitches, pick `cap` of them so each pitch
    type keeps its share of usage (largest-remainder rounding so the total is exactly
    `cap`). Returns (pitches to plot, total located)."""
    sub = sub[sub["LocSideIn"].notna() & sub["LocHeightIn"].notna()]
    n = len(sub)
    if n <= cap:
        return sub, n

    counts = sub["TaggedPitchType"].value_counts()
    exact = counts / n * cap
    quota = np.floor(exact).astype(int)
    leftover = cap - int(quota.sum())
    for pitch in (exact - quota).sort_values(ascending=False, kind="stable").index[:leftover]:
        quota[pitch] += 1

    parts = [sub[sub["TaggedPitchType"].eq(p)].sample(n=int(q), random_state=seed)
             for p, q in quota.items() if q > 0]
    return pd.concat(parts), n

title: Catcher Reports
text: These catcher reports are created and sent to our catchers and catching coach after every game. The script combines a TrackMan file with our hand-charted tracking data to produce a PDF with a one-page report for each catcher who appeared. They tell our coach how each catcher performed framing, blocking, and throwing out would-be base stealers. The report uses an expected-strike model and run expectancy based blocking and throwing runs to measure each catcher’s impact on the game.

title: Catcher Reports
text:
What’s on the page

Framing: a close-up of the strike zone with every called strike and ball in the shadow zone plotted, color coded, and labeled with expected-strike probability. Called strike rate above expected shows the catcher’s framing performance compared to the mid-major D1 average.
Blocking: blocks made and attempted with runners on, broken down by side and by pitch group, plus the runs credited for successful blocks.
Throwing: steal attempts, caught stealings, throw velocity, pop times to each base, and runs credited for caught stealings.

title: Catcher Reports
text:
The expected-strike model
To judge framing you need to know how often a pitch in a given spot should be called a strike. The report uses a location-only model; a smoothed grid of called-strike probability every 0.05 ft across the zone, trained on over 90,000 called pitches from 741 games. On a holdout set of 15,546 pitches it predicted a 33.0% strike rate against an actual 32.5% (Brier score: 0.066).
A catcher’s CStr% minus his xCStr% on a subset of pitches shows whether he’s getting more or less called strikes than the locations deserve. The model doesn’t account for the umpire or the batter’s height.

title: Catcher Reports
section: Turning blocks and throws into runs
text:
Turning blocks and throws into runs
Blocking and throwing runs created are calculated using Fangraphs’ Run Expectancy (RE) tables. A successful block is credited with the difference between the actual situation and the one where every runner moves up a base. A caught stealing is credited with the difference between the runner being safe at the base he tried for and the situation after the out. Failed blocks and successful steals count as zero, so these are totals of credit earned, not net runs saved.

title: Catcher Reports
text:
Impact
These reports are produced postgame and sent to our catchers and catching coach to look over. If a catcher struggled with his blocks on one side of the plate the previous game, his pre-game drill work the next day might focus on improving that area. If the reports consistently show that a catcher struggles receiving on one side of the plate, we might decide not to catch him when particular pitchers who work to that side often throw. The reports are used to evaluate the performance and guide the development of our catchers.

title: Catcher Reports
text:
What’s next
I plan on changing the throwing section of this report to a more actionable visual. I want to show the pitch location of each pop time plotted in the strike zone so that our catching coach gets a better idea of where a catcher’s transfer is best or needs improvement.

title: Catcher Reports
text:
Code
The run-value credit for blocks and caught stealings:


Show code

def block_credit(table, bases, outs, success):
    """Credit for a successful block: the run value of every runner NOT moving up one
    base (a runner on third would have scored). Uses only the pre-pitch base/out
    state; count, batter result and advancement odds aren't modeled. A failed block
    is worth zero (we only credit positive plays)."""
    if not success:
        return 0.0
    if not any(bases):
        raise ValueError("A block with empty bases is outside the tracked population")
    everyone_advances = (0, bases[0], bases[1])
    raw = bases[2] + expectancy(table, everyone_advances, outs) - expectancy(table, bases, outs)
    return max(0.0, raw)


def throwing_credit(table, bases, outs, targets, outcome, advance=False, out_target=None):
    """Credit for a caught stealing: run value if the runner had been safe minus the
    run value after the out. A safe steal is worth zero.
    Returns (credit, bases after, runs scored on the play)."""
    if outcome == "safe":
        after, runs = steal_result(bases, targets, advance)
        return 0.0, after, runs
    if outcome != "out":
        raise ValueError("Steal outcome must be safe or out")
    if advance:
        raise ValueError("Caught stealing plus advance on throw needs individual runner outcomes")
    if len(targets) > 1 and out_target not in targets:
        raise ValueError("A double steal with an out needs OutBase (2 or 3)")

    out_target = out_target or targets[0]
    if_safe, safe_runs = steal_result(bases, targets)
    actual, actual_runs = steal_result(bases, targets, out_target=out_target)
    credit = (safe_runs + expectancy(table, if_safe, outs)) - (actual_runs + expectancy(table, actual, outs + 1))
    return max(0.0, credit), actual, actual_runs

What’s on the page

Platoon splits: BA, OBP, SLG, wOBA, HR, K%, BB% and HBP, overall and by pitcher handedness.
Hot & cold zones: a heat map of XBH, BA vs FBs by location, and a heat map of whiffs; understand where in the zone his swing is most and least effective.
Spray charts: every ball in play plotted on a field diagram, helping the defense position themselves and understand the hitter’s bat path.
Pitch-type splits: BA, SLG, whiff rate and hard-hit rate against fastballs, breaking balls, and offspeed pitches from each handedness.
Plate approach: metrics describing 1st pitch and two strike approach, including zone swing rates, chase rates, and outcomes by pitch type.
Skills: results against 90+ mph velocity, stolen bases and bunts.
Scouting notes: my written read on his swing and how to pitch him based on video analysis and performance data.

title: Hitter Reports
text:
How it works
The script combines multiple TrackMan files and keeps only our hitters. It accounts for potential mis-tagged names with improper spacing, capitalization, or spelling. It also recognizes switch hitters and gives them a separate page for each side of the plate.
A few details:

Mid-major averages. The mid-major averages are calculated using TrackMan data from teams in the Big West, Mountain West, and West Coast conferences.
Avg max exit velocity. Comparing a hitter’s max exit velocity to the single hardest-hit ball in a 200,000 pitch file would make everyone look weak. Instead, the benchmark is the average of each D1 hitter’s personal max, among hitters with at least 20 balls in play.
Spray charts for LHH. Angles are flipped for left-handed hitters, so “pull” always means pull, and pull, middle and opposite-field rates can be compared across hitters.
Accounting for ABs/PAs correctly. TrackMan records strikeouts, walks, and hit by pitches in the KorBB column while all balls in play are recorded under PlayResult. The script accounts for this and keeps just one result-bearing pitch per plate appearance to ensure rates are calculated correctly.

title: Hitter Reports
text:
Impact
These reports were produced at the end of the fall and were reviewed with each hitter during individual exit meetings with our hitting coaches. Winter development plans were created based on the insights the reports gave. Some hitters had poor spray charts and were given drills to focus on bat path adjustments. Others had high chase rates and were given drills to improve their feel for the zone. They will be updated and produced periodically throughout the year to track the progress and guide the development of our hitters.

title: Hitter Reports
text:
Code
Every stat line on the page comes from one function:


Show code

def stat_line(pas):
    """AVG / OBP / SLG / OPS / wOBA / HR for a set of plate-appearance-ending pitches."""
    result = pas["PlayResult"]
    singles = (result == "Single").sum()
    doubles = (result == "Double").sum()
    triples = (result == "Triple").sum()
    hr = (result == "HomeRun").sum()
    bb = (pas["KorBB"] == "Walk").sum()
    hbp = (pas["PitchCall"] == "HitByPitch").sum()
    sac = (result == "Sacrifice").sum()

    hits = singles + doubles + triples + hr
    at_bats = len(pas) - bb - hbp - sac
    total_bases = singles + 2 * doubles + 3 * triples + 4 * hr
    obp_denominator = at_bats + bb + hbp + sac

    avg = hits / at_bats if at_bats else 0
    slg = total_bases / at_bats if at_bats else 0
    obp = (hits + bb + hbp) / obp_denominator if len(pas) else 0

    w = WOBA_WEIGHTS
    woba_numerator = (w["BB"] * bb + w["HBP"] * hbp + w["1B"] * singles
                      + w["2B"] * doubles + w["3B"] * triples + w["HR"] * hr)
    woba = woba_numerator / obp_denominator if len(pas) else 0

    return {"PA": len(pas), "AVG": round(avg, 3), "OBP": round(obp, 3),
            "SLG": round(slg, 3), "OPS": round(obp + slg, 3),
            "wOBA": round(woba, 3), "HR": hr}
